newsitem.title: USA: PSCO, SPS see no bar to US FERC approval of merger.
newsitem.headline: PSCO, SPS see no bar to US FERC approval of merger.

text.p: Public Service Co of Colorado and Southwestern Public Service Co said they see no obstacles to winning approval Wednesday from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission for their planned merger.
"There are no longer any intervenors (in the case)," Southwestern spokesman Ken Vaughn said Tuesday.
"We're ready to get this merger done this spring....We feel very good," he said.
The commission is scheduled to discuss the merger, valued at $4 billion, at its regular meeting Wednesday.
The proposed merger to create New Century Energies has already won state approvals, and only requires nods from the FERC and the Securities and Exchange Commission to go ahead.

FERC commissioners last year raised concern that the plan did not protect customers from rate increases resulting from merger costs and raised concern that the merger might stifle competition in bulk power markets in the Southwest.
Those issues were addressed in a settlement between the companies and all but one of the groups that had filed complaints.
The settlement was endorsed by a FERC administrative law judge in December, clearing the way for the commission to decide on the merger.
PSC of Colorado also reached an agreement with the last intervenor, the Colorado Association of Municipal Utilities, which had concerns about wholesale power in Colorado.
While the companies would not predict how the commission would rule Wednesday, a spokeswoman for PSC of Colorado said the judge's green light "gives us something to go on."
PSC of Colorado serves Colorado and Wyoming and Southwestern serves Southwestern operating in Texas, New Mexico, Oklahoma and Kansas.
